questions.q: In crow's-foot notation, a line between Account and Contact with a single tick at the Account end and a three-pronged crow's foot at the Contact end means:
options: Many Accounts relate to many Contacts
One Account relates to many Contacts, and each Contact relates to exactly one Account
One Account relates to exactly one Contact
Contacts cannot be related to Accounts at all
questions.explain: The single tick (at Account) means 'one'; the crow's foot (at Contact) means 'many' — so one Account can have many Contacts, and each Contact belongs to exactly one Account, matching a standard Salesforce lookup.

questions.q: Why does a many-to-many relationship need a junction object, both in Salesforce and on the ERD?
options: Because Salesforce has no native many-to-many relationship type; the junction object implements it as two one-to-many relationships, one to each side
Because junction objects are required by GDPR for any custom object
Because a direct many-to-many line is always drawn on ERDs and never needs a junction object
Because crow's-foot notation cannot represent 'many' on both ends of a line
questions.explain: Salesforce only provides lookup and master-detail, both one-to-many at the data level — a many-to-many relationship is built from a junction object holding two one-to-many relationships, and the ERD should show that same two-hop structure.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does it matter whether a one-to-many Salesforce relationship is implemented as lookup vs. master-detail, even though both appear as the same crow's-foot line on an ERD?
options: It doesn't matter — lookup and master-detail behave identically in every respect
Master-detail cascades delete of the parent to its children and enables roll-up summary fields; lookup does neither, so a plain line can't tell a reviewer which behavior to expect
Lookup relationships are always many-to-many, while master-detail is always one-to-one
Master-detail relationships cannot be shown on an ERD at all
questions.explain: Lookup and master-detail are both one-to-many structurally, but master-detail adds cascading delete and roll-up summary support that lookup doesn't — a real behavioral difference the diagram alone doesn't capture, which is why annotation matters.

questions.q: What does this lesson say an ERD deliberately leaves out?
options: Entities and their attributes
Relationship cardinality
Automation, page layouts, and security — everything that isn't data structure
Entity names
questions.explain: An ERD's narrowness is deliberate: it shows the shape of the data model (entities, attributes, relationships) and nothing else, so automation, UI, and security layers don't clutter a reader's understanding of the structure.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say Salesforce's native Schema Builder is not, by itself, architecture documentation?
options: Schema Builder cannot display custom objects
Schema Builder requires a paid add-on license to function
It's useful for exploring the live object model, but it can't be annotated with the reasoning behind a relationship and historically hasn't offered a clean way to export a finished, versioned diagram
Schema Builder is identical to a written solution design document
questions.explain: Schema Builder shows the current state of the org's object model live, which is valuable for exploration, but it doesn't capture the 'why' behind a relationship or produce a durable, exportable, versioned artifact the way dedicated diagramming tools do.
